reviews.author: WANGYOUNG LEE
reviews.text:
Near JR stations such as Tokyo's Akihabara, Okachimachi, and Kinshicho, there are a lot of yakitori restaurants that constantly emit thick smoke and an unpleasant smell.

Of course, I've been to Shimbashi, Ikebukuro and Iidabashi, but the atmosphere is quite different. Among the places I've been to, Akihabara is memorable for its fire power, taste, and hospitality.

There was also a Korean part-time worker there. He said he wanted to learn skills there and open a yakitori restaurant when he returns to Korea, and he provided a lot of service.

That was in December 2019, and from March 2020, I could no longer go to Japan, and my separation from Japan began. I missed yakitori so I visited Yuda in Dongbu Ichon-dong.

I went around May 2020, so it was already 2 years and 2 months ago. I encountered Yakitori in Myeongdong, which I had forgotten about for a long time. I found it when I stayed at Solaria in May, but I couldn't go there then.

I already had chicken and beer at the nutrition center, so I wasn't craving it. Then, this time, I planned a staycation in Myeongdong again and visited this place. It was a little after 10 p.m.

For dinner, I made a simple Chungmu Gimbap and ate it with affogato from Byeoldabang branch to empty my stomach. And when we arrived, the tables were full even though it was a weekday.

Fortunately, the 4 counter seats were empty and I took one without waiting. I wanted to shout ‘Toria Eznama’ like in my home country, but~~~!

Instead, just ask for a glass of Asahi draft beer. Yakitori can be ordered individually, and there is also omakase, so I order 5 types. Edamame (peas) is also ordered additionally.

Since it is a counter seat, you can directly see the skewers being grilled. It's a visual that seems to have been imported from Japan. The firepower of charcoal fire is not as good as that of Japan.

Still, it looks quite plausible. The edamame is blanched right away, so it retains its warmth. This cools down quickly over time.

As I'm eating edamame at Asahi, the yakitori I'm going to eat is being grilled. After a while, he gave me a seat right away. Like holding sushi!

The chef seems a bit Japanese, but his Korean pronunciation is clear, so he seems Korean. Later, when I was paying the bill, another employee (the boss) said that he had been living in Japan for a long time.

Suntory was not imported, so I drank Jim Beam Highball as my second drink in a Suntory glass and the last drink as sake in a Tokuri glass. Yakitori is also decent at this level.

On this day, we stayed at a Japanese hotel chain, starting with check-in information, receiving guidance from Japanese staff, and even yakitori! The day ended on a good note. thank you

reviews.text:
I arrived at the subway station after a hard day's work, but for some reason I didn't want to get on the train at Euljiro 1-ga Station, so I trudged along the underground passage toward Euljiro 3-ga Station and found a strangely dark but cozy-looking restaurant and went in.

When I entered, the store with the fragrant scent of Shiso wafting around me, I saw that they were selling a variety of Japanese home-cooked menu items. I had a hard time deciding between tendon and futomaki & tamago sushi and decided on the latter. As I was in a good mood, I also ordered a bottle of beer.

As I was drinking a beer, the menu I ordered was immediately presented to me. The meal served neatly on a tray felt like home cooking. Futomaki had a good texture of shiso, salmon, cucumber, egg, and even slightly soggy fries, and was clean and tidy without being spicy.

The tamago sushi didn't taste as special as it looked, but it was soft and moist. Shiso, pork, lotus root, burdock, radish, and other ingredients are all served with soybean paste soup that has been boiled until soft.

On a stressful day, I couldn't relieve my stress with spicy food, but it was a nice evening because I felt like I was receiving some warm comfort. I think I will often think of this on my way home from work when I am stressed.

reviews.text:
The word and visual of Kodonburu, which exudes old-fashioned sensibility, that I saw in Kimisanggung's review last time reminded me of Myeongdong Donkatsu, which I visited a few times in the past, long before more luxurious tonkatsu shops like today were established. It brought back great memories. I visited a little after 2pm, when it seemed to be a bit free after lunch time, but it was in vain because it was open for lunch until 2pm, so I decided to stop by again today in time for lunch.

I had already been to the store once before, so I knew the location, but as I was getting closer to the store, I passed the intersection in front of the Jungbu Police Station that was featured in the girl group GFriend's new music video for Crossroads. As a fan of Godja Friend, I felt like I was making a quick pilgrimage, so I took a picture around where Eunha was standing in the music video, and as I approached the store, there were office workers waiting, so I asked if they would take a numbered ticket, and they told me to go inside, talk to them, place an order in advance, and wait. I went inside, ordered Los Gas and waited outside.

While waiting, I looked at the menu picture outside the store and it looked like it was a B set menu with fish, loin, and shrimp gas, so the size looked a little small, but I was curious so I went inside the store and asked if I could change the menu. I was told that I could get a set meal with hiregasu, but not a set meal with loach gas. Since today was my first visit, I decided to just try the locust.

The store is located in an alley that gives off an Euljiro feel, but I just wish the exterior of the store was a little prettier.

Perhaps because the customer turnover rate was high, about 6-7 customers in front entered one after another, and soon it was my turn and I was guided to a table for two and sat down.

The store is famous, with many famous people's autographs on the walls.

First, warm corn tea was served in a plastic cup, and since the order had been placed in advance, Los Gas came out quickly.

The Rosgas is plated with a classic feel, just like the one that made me want to go to Take last time. There are two pieces of cucumber and a little sliced ​​red cabbage on top of shredded white cabbage, so the color contrast gives off a classic feel. Mustard, pickled radish, and jinzuke are on top. The Rosgas is cut horizontally and vertically, and although it is not as thick as I like, it is cut to a more popular size, so it still has a classic feel.

Kakdugi (radish radish kimchi) was also served, but I couldn't taste it because I didn't taste it. The miso soup was thin and bland, and the rice was so small that I could eat it all in 3 servings since I scooped it with chopsticks, so I asked for a refill of the cabbage salad and rice later.

The salad dressing that I expected to be a little different was just an ordinary sesame dressing. I sprinkled the pork cutlet sauce over the mustard, mixed it well, took a piece of loin cutlet, and tasted it. The batter was moist with a little bit of the oil I like, but it didn't feel like bread crumbs. The oil was drained enough and the three-dimensionality was low, so it was flat, so it wasn't impressive, but the sirloin had a lot of tender meat, so it was chewy rather than being cut smoothly. It's good because the meat is tender enough to taste good, but it's not too thick, so it doesn't have the juicy feel of premium tonkatsu, but the less thick breadcrumb coating and moderately chewy sirloin feel a little closer to the feel of Japanese tonkatsu than the Korean type of rich pork cutlet last time.

I thought it would be okay to sprinkle salt on it, so I asked for salt. The kitchen brought some salt, sprinkled it on, and when I tasted it, it wasn't awkward and was okay, so I sprinkled salt on it rather than the pork cutlet sauce.

Although I don't like Kodonburu in general, I liked the Kodonburu menu and the nostalgic visual plating, so I stopped by Myeong Donkatsu. Although it is on a different level from the premium tonkatsu that is popular these days, it was still nice to be able to taste the classic style of porkcutt that everyone used to know as Japanese pork cutlet in the city at a relatively reasonable price. It's not a special restaurant, so it's not enough to visit, but when I go nearby, it tastes more like old-fashioned Japanese tonkatsu than closer to Korean. If you want to taste pork cutlet, it's worth stopping by..

While walking down the streets of Las Vegas to digest food after the first meal, I stumbled upon the menu item ‘Nikudofu’ written on the signboard of an izakaya that caught my eye, so I waited without hesitation. When I arrived around 7pm on a Friday night, there was one group in front of me, and I had to wait about 40 minutes before I could enter. At first I was concerned about the long waiting time, but in the end it was well worth the wait.

As soon as I entered the store, I felt a cozy and comfortable atmosphere, and the staff were friendly, so I was able to start my meal in a good mood. The menu items I ordered were stir-fried chicken skin and eggplant, Nikudofu (standard size), and Monaca matcha ice cream for dessert. All of the menu items were better than expected, and the nikudoufu was especially impressive with its deep, rich flavor. The combination of gently cooked meat and flavorful broth was perfect to eat with rice.

The stir-fried eggplant with chicken skin had a crunchy yet moist texture, and the softness of the eggplant and harmonious taste made it perfect as a side dish for drinks. Lastly, the Monaca Matcha Ice Cream had a clean yet rich matcha flavor, making it the perfect choice to end the meal. Overall, the quality of the food was high, I could feel the sincerity in the cooking process, and I was very satisfied to be able to experience this quality of Japanese cuisine in Las Vegas.

I highly recommend it to anyone looking for an izakaya, and I definitely want to visit again next time. It's a great place to enjoy delicious food while having a quick drink, as well as for special occasions!

Konbu (4.2/5.0) - When you want to eat vongole and Japanese ramen at the same time.

One-line review: Sakaba, a small but happy ramen that can be found in the alleys of Euljiro like a treasure hunt.

"Euljiro Alley"
There is a small ramen restaurant in one of the crowded alleys of Euljiro, one of the most difficult to find. If you want to go here, I recommend marching north from the 'Intersection in front of Jungbu Police Station' and entering the first alley. As you enter the alley, a large red sign with '昆布 (Konbu, Kelp)' written on it will let you know that you have reached your destination. Jiyuken, a nearby Japanese-style Chinese restaurant, is also known to have the same origin.

As the self-introduction of the restaurant called Ramensakaba (ラーメン酒場) suggests, it sells mainly ramen food during the day, but transforms into an izakaya focusing on alcoholic beverages in the evening. It consists of only 14 counter seats and is a pleasant place filled with deep green chopsticks and cute accessories. The classic album 'NewJeans' stands out. Please note that the composition and prices of the weekday daytime menu and weekend and nighttime menus are slightly different. The price of 'Karaguchi Shoyu Ramen' during the day on weekdays is 12,000 won, but at other times it goes up to 13,900 won. The 6,000 won side menu ‘100% beef croquette’ is also available only during the day on weekdays.

"Clam broth"
This restaurant's signature 'Karaguchi Shoyu Ramen' is a quite special menu that combines the flavor of clams and the spicy taste of rayu. Just like 'Vongole Shoyu Ramen', this is a version of ramen that uses a double broth blended with kelp broth and clam broth on a soy sauce base, and adds ray oil to maximize the spicy aroma and umami. Some say it tastes spicier than 'Shin Ramyun', but I personally think it's a little spicier than that. However, it's not something you can get excited about. It is not a spicy soup that hurts your tongue, but a pleasant spicy taste that makes you sweat.

As soon as it comes out, I put the 'Aji Tamago (Japanese-style braised egg) aside and take a bite of the soup. Rayu's unique oily and spicy scent is felt first, followed by the subtle sweetness of chives and onions, along with the smell of the sea from the clams. Even if it is called vongole, it tastes like the sea. Eat the perfectly opened clam meat with the soup and enjoy the unique savory taste. The amount of thin 'Hosomen' is a bit small, and the cooking level is extremely tight.

“Toppings and sides”
The two chicken tenderloin toppings are very tender and tasty. Menma (bamboo shoots) is smooth and has a nice texture, and the flavor spreads well in your mouth. Two pieces of wide and thin pork char siu are placed around the top of the bowl. Four points are given in the evening and on weekends. It has a strong meaty flavor and a slight odor, but it doesn't bother me too much. I tried soaking the meat in the spicy broth and eating it, but it's a bit difficult to say that the two are perfectly harmonious.

Taking a break from ramen, I turn my attention to the side menu. The '100% Beef Croquette' is made with two pieces of minced beef coated in a suitable batter and cut in half, making a total of four pieces. The juicy meat is covered with mayo sauce. The juiciness of the meat bursts with the sweetness and freshness of the onion slices underneath, making it truly a delicacy.

Back to ramen. 'Ajitamago (Japanese-style braised egg)' is very satisfying as the yolk flows out just enough and mixes perfectly with the soup. Like any other ramen restaurant, they provide free bowls of rice to customers who want it, and when mixed with Karaguchi shoyu ramen broth, the appearance and taste are similar to those of eating Korean instant ramen with rice. When ordering rice, we recommend that you order it in advance and let it cool down at least a few minutes before rolling it to maximize the flavor of the soup.

'Konbu' is a pleasant ramen restaurant filled with sincerity and a witty atmosphere for its special ramen.

It was the weekend and I wanted to eat something delicious, so I looked around and found a sukiyaki restaurant. I was looking for a variety of food that didn't put a burden on my stomach, but had a variety of courses...Ageru, a sukiyaki restaurant that was perfect for me who likes shabu. It's difficult to say there was anything special about it, but overall I was satisfied!

The inside of the store I entered was very clean. When you come in, you can see at a glance that the structural lighting is bright yet moderately subtle, and tables for 2 to 4 people are appropriately placed.

Vegetables were set on the table as a basic table setting. It looked like they had been prepared and arranged in advance, but they were fresh. It was just the right amount for two people to enjoy. I was drinking a highball in advance, hoping that the broth would boil for a delicious meal. The price of 1+1 10,000 won was very attractive. It was a sour Santorini highball ~

The shabu-shabu sauce has a soy sauce base and a sour taste, a bit like ponzu sauce. It has the right tantalizing taste. I also took out vegetables that were ripe enough to eat on the plate. It may be too hot, so let it cool down later.

Next, eat sukiyaki dipped in eggs ;;; Oh ㅏㅏㅏ I really like raw eggs. The meat is thin and soft, soaked in soy sauce, and the egg really brings out the flavor. It's really my style 😥👍 It tastes even more delicious when served with vegetables. There are a variety of enoki mushrooms, bok choy, bean sprouts, and cabbage.

I liked both the shabu shabu and sukiyaki broth. The shabu is light and has a smoothness that allows you to taste each ingredient more. The sukiyaki has a slightly richer broth than the shabu. It simply has a strong salty taste, so the combination of the ingredients with the seaweed and egg dipped in it was so fantastic! Personally, I think I'll be looking for sukiyaki again to eat it.

Next, the meal is somewhat finished and it's time to enjoy udon. You can choose between curry or poached egg soy sauce, but I thought curry would taste better for some reason, so I asked for it! Although it is not a solid curry, they added a proper curry sauce to the broth that is definitely different from instant curry. I enjoyed it so much, but I can't believe I can still eat udon! That's why I like shabu-type food ~ The flow of the meal is so beautiful... The curry is moderately seasoned and the menu is of high quality. Even though I was full, I still ate the plump noodles. There were still some vegetables left, so I ate them together. The atmosphere was good ~ This is a satisfactory review of Ageru, a sukiyaki restaurant in Euljiro where I met a friend after a long time and enjoyed a delicious meal.

A restaurant with a nice atmosphere, good service, and even better food. I recommend Euljiro for family gatherings, company dinners, and dates. I like all Jingawa stores, but I especially like the Euljiro branch.

reviews.author: jinhee kim
reviews.text:
I visited with a friend after a long time because I was craving Japanese dining with a nice atmosphere. I ordered the Bangawa course and I was very satisfied!

The first course was milk-based mushroom buckwheat noodles. I ate it without any expectations, but was surprised by the deliciousness! First of all, the sauce is so delicious and the buckwheat noodles are chewy!!!
The second bite dish comes with fried lotus root, salad, eggplant, etc. Does the taste really awaken your appetite?
The sashimi included mackerel tataki, salmon, flounder fin, tuna, yellowtail, and red sea bream, all of which were fresh.
Tempura was also served, and even my friend who didn't like fried food enjoyed it. It was crazy to see the vegetable juices bursting out of the eggplant. Afterwards, after eating all the soft soup, vegetables, and meat with the miso nabe, I felt like my stomach was going to explode... The last thing that comes out is cotton sari? But it was so delicious that I couldn't stop using chopsticks even when I was full haha.

Ice cream was served for dessert, and it ended so well that I wanted to eat another one. When I left, I got some cute Halloween-only candy and went for a walk along Cheonggyecheon with my friend!

reviews.author: jinwoo Chae
reviews.text: Bamboo Aging Hall near Jonggak Station is a restaurant specializing in fermented raw fish with a comfortable atmosphere with soft lighting and bamboo decorations. Partitions and wide seat spacing make it great for quiet dining. The maturation space provided at the entrance has detailed maturation times and dates for each type of fish, giving a sense of trust. The maturation sashimi consists of red sea bream, flounder, salmon, and tataki, and the natural flow of flavors is impressive. Two types of soy sauce with different sweetness and saltiness were provided so you could choose according to the type of fish, and the flavors of monkfish liver and tataki fish added interest to the composition, creating a good overall balance. The seasoning for the Chori-ri-bap was not overly seasoned, so it went well with the texture of the fish, and the Spicy Seafood Soup, which I ordered to end the meal, was rich in fish and roe, and the spicy yet not overpowering taste of the soup was satisfying. Overall, I had a strong feeling that it was a good place to enjoy aged raw fish and warm soup together in a quiet atmosphere.

reviews.author: Ji Kyeong-woo
reviews.text:
Izakaya located between Jonggak and Gwanghwamun.

I wonder if a Japanese person runs the store. The serving staff also seem to be made up of Japanese people.

The store is located in the very back of the basement, so if it's your first visit, you might get a little lost. When you visit, you will get a strong exotic feeling from the Japanese greetings and unfamiliar interior. (There is even NHK Japan news on TV.)

There are izakaya-style seats that can seat four people, and there appears to be a separate room.

Japanese servers help you with seating information and food ordering, but it really makes you feel like you're in Japan, so be careful if you have anxiety about foreigners.

The food is not good value for money. It had great taste through good ingredients, but the quantity felt a bit small compared to the price.

Therefore, it is judged that it is best to visit this place as a second or third visit. However, the store is open until 9:30 p.m. and orders close at 9 p.m., so if you go at an odd time, you may find yourself in a dilemma.

If you want to feel the atmosphere of a Japanese tavern, I recommend visiting this place at least once.

Pretty Spicy Gyoza 6p 4,000
Since the price of ramen is over 10,000 won, I had high expectations for the quality! There was a reason it was famous. First of all, the amount of char siu was huge, so I was more satisfied than other ramen restaurants where I was disappointed with the char siu I ate every time I ate it, and the types of char siu were also novel because they consisted of beef pork and pork. The beef pork chashu had a new taste when I dipped it into the soup to see if it had been seasoned.
I ordered the gyoza spicy, and at 4,000 won for 6 pieces, I thought it was good value for money, and it went well with the ramen. The spiciness felt a little artificial, but it was still delicious.
And since I personally am a fan of kimchi, I also liked that the ramen restaurant had kimchi prepared😍

There was quite a lot of meat and the ramen itself was large overall.
If you order a set meal, they also serve rice, which is another fun part.

Taste 6 Price 5 Quantity 5 Friendliness 5 (total score 5)

It's not just about sushi, but various signature dishes are placed between courses to slowly open your palate.

Stimulate your taste buds more thoroughly with dishes that train the scent and texture carefully arranged between courses.

*Impressive part
Truffle salt, very soft driver's uniform, sea urchin cream, mawa truffle, garlic or shiso on sushi, minced tuna wrapped in tofu, sweet pumpkin-like eggplant, cheonggukjang pot rice

The course is highly regarded for not only providing sushi, but also discovering new gourmet dishes through research.
Even though it is a restaurant where reservations are very difficult and repeat visits are difficult, I thought that the service of allowing visiting customers to make their next reservations on site first was a unique concept.

Young people can come no matter how difficult it is through competition for catch tables, but it was impressive to be able to convey the impression to other generations by making on-site reservations for parts that may be difficult for parents' generation, so it was impressive that, unlike other omakase, there were a few elderly people.

The service aspect is also highly regarded, and even though it is difficult to cater to each and every person, even for omakase, I felt very comfortable in the leisurely manner in which everything is catered for when a single person requests it.

This is my second visit to the Nonde Series along with Tuna Nonde, and I personally hope that the Nonde Series will become more prosperous and more numerous in many aspects.
